# Sizing a power station for a fridge

You need to clear three numbers, and the surge rating is the one that most often trips people up.

| Check | What to look for |
|---|---|
| **Surge watts** | At least **1,300 W** to cover the compressor startup. Typical fridges spike to roughly 1,000-2,400 W ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)). |
| **Continuous watts** | A full-size fridge runs at about 100-250 W, so any ~1,000 W-class station covers it. |
| **Watt-hours** | Depends on how long the outage lasts (see below). |

Also make sure the unit has **pure sine wave** output, which is standard on reputable LiFePO4 stations.

## Capacity by outage length

The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages far less than its running watts.

- **About 1,000 Wh** runs a typical fridge for roughly 17 hours ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- **About 1,400 Wh** covers a full 24 hours, including inverter losses and 20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
- **About 2,000 Wh** gives roughly 33 hours to 1.4 days.
- **About 2,800 Wh** is needed for two days, and about 4,200 Wh for three.

For a closer number, check the yellow EnergyGuide label on your fridge. Take kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 for average watts, then multiply by hours and add roughly 40% for losses and headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)). A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average about twice the ENERGY STAR figure, and a warm kitchen or frequent door-opening also raises it. Keep the door shut during the outage.

## Options that fit

- **BLUETTI AC200L** (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, 3,600 W surge) is rated around 33 hours for a fridge, and you can add expansion batteries later. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF according to Dealectric's cart test. [Buy at BLUETTI via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Details are on the [product page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l).
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak) is listed at $699.99 after coupon. See the [Anker SOLIX guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator).
- **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak) is a good pick if you only need about a day or less. It was recently seen at $399-699 ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (1,070 Wh) covers about 17 hours and was recently seen at $449-799 ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

I didn't get direct purchase links for the AC180 or Jackery, so use the guide pages above to find current prices. Prices change, so confirm at checkout. Small units under about 300 Wh generally fail the surge check and aren't suited to a full-size fridge.

**Bottom line:** For a typical fridge, a 1,000-1,500 Wh station with at least 1,300 W of surge covers about a day. Choose around 2,000 Wh or more if outages in your area run longer, or if you want to power other essentials too.
